def: The keys and values of all earlier tokens, saved at every layer so each new token's attention does not recompute them.
The first phase of serving, in which the whole prompt is processed in one parallel pass before any token is generated.
The generation phase, one token per step, in which each step reads the weights and the whole KV cache and is limited by memory bandwidth.
Attention with many query heads but a single shared key head and value head, which shrinks the KV cache by the number of heads.
Attention in which groups of query heads share one key/value head, a dial between multi-head and multi-query attention.
Converting an existing multi-head checkpoint to grouped-query attention with a small fraction of the original training compute.
Causal attention in which each token reads only its previous W tokens, so scored pairs grow as T times W instead of T squared.
A KV cache of fixed size W that overwrites slot position mod W, valid because tokens older than the window are never read again.
How far back a token can be influenced, which for windowed attention is about the number of layers times W minus one.
The first tokens of a sequence, where softmax puts weight that no content deserves, and which a sliding window should keep.
High-bandwidth memory, the large main memory of a GPU, much bigger and slower than its on-chip SRAM.
A softmax computed block by block with a running maximum and sum that are rescaled as new blocks arrive, giving the exact result.
An exact attention kernel that works tile by tile in on-chip memory and never writes the full score matrix to HBM.
